Edges at A (degrees 2 and 3) give -0.41, edges between degree-3 nodes -0.33, and the highlighted D–E (3 and 1) -0.58." width="100%"} The normalized Laplacian `D^-½ (D - A) D^-½` rescales each entry by the degrees of its endpoints, so that high-degree nodes do not dominate. Its eigenvalues always lie in `[0, 2]` (with `2` only for bipartite components), which makes spectra comparable across graphs of different sizes and densities; it is the matrix behind normalized spectral clustering (Shi-Malik, Ng-Jordan-Weiss) and is closely tied to random walks on the graph. Isolated nodes get an all-zero row and column. Matches NetworkX's `normalized_laplacian_matrix()`; its eigenvalues are `laplacian_spectrum(normalized=True)`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[list[list[float]], list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(matrix, node_ids)`: the matrix as a list of rows, and the node IDs labelling rows and columns, in increasing order. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Diagonal entries are `1` for every node with edges: ::: {#1b1396d3 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(3) matrix, nodes = path.normalized_laplacian_matrix() [[round(v, 3) for v in row] for row in matrix] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [[1.0, -0.707, 0.0], [-0.707, 1.0, -0.707], [0.0, -0.707, 1.0]] ``` ::: :::
